To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the observed Hα line profile of the source star of the binary micolensing event OGLE-2003-BUL-69, as the star is leaving the caustic of the lens, is well described by a model atmosphere of a cool giant.
we have detected a chromospheric flare from the source star during the microlensing event and we have measured the size of the chromosphere to be 0.3 R*.

we have obtained a high-resolution spectrum of a G5III star in the bulge of the Milky Way, and we have detected the amplified emission from the star\'s chromosphere as the star\'s trailing edge exited a microlensing caustic.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of high-resolution time-resolved spectra obtained during a microlensing event.

the use of microlensing to probe the atmosphere of a giant star, and the application of a high-resolution, time series spectroscopic technique to study the chromosphere and the photospheric line profile of a giant star.
the study of the stellar atmosphere of an evolved G giant in the Bulge.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have detected a chromosphere in a giant star.
the NextGEN model atmosphere is in good agreement with the observations.

our observations of the H alpha line during the OGLE-2006-BUL-69 event have provided a new insight into the structure of the atmosphere of a giant star, and that the microlensing technique can be used to obtain such information.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to obtain a detailed view on the atmosphere of an old giant in the bulge of our Galaxy, which is a rare case in astronomy.
we were able to obtain the first time-resolved spectra for the atmosphere of an old G5 giant star.
the observed spectra of OGLE-2003-BUL-069 are consistent with the NextGEN model atmosphere, but there is a need to include chromosphere effects in the model.
The main takeaway from our work is that

high-resolution spectroscopy of microlensing events is now feasible, and that the combination of high-resolution spectroscopy, photometry, and modelling will allow us to probe the structure and dynamics of stars in unprecedented detail.
the OGLE-3 Early Warning System has provided a unique opportunity to probe the atmosphere of a giant star in the bulge.

microlensing provides a unique way of probing the atmospheres of stars in distant galaxies, and that the combination of photometric and spectroscopic observations can be very effective in constraining stellar atmosphere models.
